catalog_quote: Guininaang has eighteen segmental phonemes and at least one supra-segmental phonemic contrast. ... The suprasegmental phonemic contrast is in stress. ... 3.3 Stress has not been fully studied as yet; therefore, little more than its phonemic status can be declared at this point. Examples of its contrast are these: bálat [p¹áłat] 'banana' / balát [p¹ałát] 'soup', 'broth'; káwa or qáwa [káwa] or [qáwa] 'means for suspending jars away from rats, etc.' / kawá or qawá [kawá] or [qawá] 'spider'; sánga [sáŋa] 'anger' / sangá [saŋá] 'branch'

audit.reasoning: (1) Quote check: the deciding quotation is verbatim in the held Gieser 1958 scan at sec. 1 and sec. 3.3, printed p. 19, as the locator says (page image read). (2) Deciding source is a 1958 12-page SIL phonemic article by the variety's principal describer; Glottolog lists no reference grammar or later independent phonology for lubu1243 (the non-Gieser 'grammar_sketch' entries are spurious title matches), and the author's own 1987 phonology appendix, fetched sources now from archive.org (ERIC microfiche of SPL Philippine Texts 4, p. 116), restates stress as 'significant' with four minimal pairs (bálat/balát, sánga/sangá, áwit/awít, áwa/awá) and adds (p. 126) a morphologically conditioned stress-on-reduplicant contrast — fully consistent with the 'lexical' (contrastive, no positional rule) coding. (3) Remaining unheld items are Gieser 1972 Phonetica (paywalled DOI 10.1159/000259383) and the 1963 SI

sources.quote: p.116: '2. Stress, written with an acute accent, is also significant, as illustrated by the following minimal pairs: bálat 'banana' versus balát 'broth'; sánga 'anger' versus sangá 'branch'; áwit 'fishhook' versus awít 'burden, load'; áwa 'means for suspending things away from rats' versus awá 'spider''. p.126: in the man- + C1V1- + root construction meaning 'process/procedure' 'it is to be noted that stress occurs on the reduplicated syllable', contrasting with three other constructions 'that have the same reduplication but without stress on the reduplicated syllable'.
sources.locator: Appendix C: Phonology, printed p. 116 (PDF p. 128), sec. 2; Appendix I: Morphological Constructions, printed p. 126 (PDF p. 138)
sources.note: Same author's later phonology appendix restates contrastive stress with four minimal pairs and adds a morphologically conditioned stress contrast in CV-reduplication; gives the record a second, later confirming source beyond the 1958 'not fully studied' statement.
